sections.h2: Where is Stamford, Connecticut, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Stamford is a city in Fairfield County on Long Island Sound, 34 miles from New York City. It had 135,470 residents in the 2020 census, which makes it Connecticut's second-largest city after Bridgeport.

It is also the state's largest city by area. The table gives the basic figures from Wikipedia and the Census Bureau.

FactFigure
CountyFairfield
2020 population135,470
Total area52.09 square miles
Land / water37.62 / 14.41 square miles
Distance to Hartford79 miles
Incorporated as a city1893
Public schools13 elementary, 5 middle, 3 high

Stamford borders Greenwich to the west, Darien to the east, New Canaan to the northeast and Pound Ridge, New York to the north.

Stamford has about 45 distinct neighborhoods and villages, and prices and house styles vary a lot between them. Wikipedia names these among them: Cove, East Side, Downtown, North Stamford, Glenbrook, West Side, Turn of River, Waterside, Springdale, Belltown, Ridgeway, Newfield, South End, Shippan, Roxbury and Palmers Hill.

North of the Merritt Parkway is North Stamford, the largest section by land and the least densely populated. Cove Island, off the southern shoreline, is a prominent beach and recreation area, Glenbrook and Springdale have stations on the New Canaan branch rail line, and the South End includes the Harbor Point development.

When you describe your house to a buyer, name the neighborhood. A buyer picturing a condo near the train station is not looking for the same thing as a buyer who wants an acre north of the Merritt.

Corporate headquarters drive it. As of 2023, Wikipedia reports eight Fortune 500 companies based in Stamford, and the city has the largest financial district in the New York region outside New York City.

  • Companies with headquarters in the city include Charter Communications, Philip Morris International, Synchrony Financial, Indeed, Webster Bank, United Rentals, Gartner, Pitney Bowes and WWE.
  • Major sectors are financial services, real estate, information technology, healthcare, telecommunications and retail.
  • UConn Stamford and Sacred Heart University's physician assistant program give the city a higher education presence.

The 2023 median household income was $106,552, and the 2022 per capita income of $58,297 was the highest of any city in Connecticut. Relocation and corporate moves keep some houses changing hands, and a seller with a transfer date often needs a firm closing day.

sections.h2: How does Stamford's housing mix affect sellers?
sections.html:
Stamford has more renters than owners. Wikipedia's 2018 estimates put the owner-occupied rate at 46.6 percent and the renter rate at 53.4 percent, with 54,513 housing units.

Building has been heavy downtown and on the waterfront. Harbor Point is an 80-acre mixed-use project south of downtown, planned for six million square feet of residential, retail, office and hotel space plus a marina, and the city issued permits for 4,341 housing units from 2008 to 2017.

For a seller of a single-family house, that means your buyer pool includes owner-occupants, small landlords who see the city's large renter share, and investors. For a seller of a two-family or small multifamily property, tenant status is the main thing to sort out before a sale.

sections.h2: What does Stamford's coastal weather mean for a house?
sections.html:
Stamford is on the Sound, with a temperate climate and about 51.6 inches of precipitation a year. It averages about 34 inches of snow, lower than inland Hartford, and about 15 snowy days.

Tropical storms are infrequent, but they have hit the coast. Wikipedia lists hurricane landfalls on the Connecticut coast in 1903, 1938, 1944, 1954, 1960, 1985 and 2012 (Sandy).

  • Waterfront and low-lying parcels deserve a flood zone check with your insurance agent, since the city has 14.41 square miles of water.
  • Basements in low-lying areas should be inspected for past water entry.
  • Wet snow and rain mixes in winter stress roofs and gutters.

Federal flood maps and insurance rules change, so rely on your lender or insurer for the current status of your parcel.

sections.h2: How do trains and highways help Stamford homes sell?
sections.html:
Stamford has the second-busiest station on the Metro-North system after Grand Central Terminal. Its trains run on the New Haven Line, the average nonstop commute is 47 minutes, and the first Grand Central departure is at 4:43 a.m.

Amtrak's Acela and Northeast Regional trains also stop here, and Interstate 95 and the Merritt Parkway cross the city. CT Transit buses leave from a terminal next to the train station on State Street.

Walking distance to the station is one of the strongest selling points in Stamford, so put the distance in your listing or in the information you give a cash buyer. Houses far from the station depend more on highway access and school boundaries, which are managed by Stamford Public Schools, a district of 16,212 students in 2022-23.

sections.h2: What does the seller owe when a Stamford house sells?
sections.html:
The seller pays Connecticut's conveyance tax, one percent of the price on most homes. That is 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the city under Section 12-494 (Chapter 223).

Where a Stamford price passes $800,000, the higher bracket applies. The state rate is 1.25 percent on the part of a residential price from $800,000 to $2.5 million, and 2.25 percent on the part above that. On a $1.5 million sale, the combined tax is $18,500: $6,000 plus $8,750 to the state on the two slices, and $3,750 to the city.

The grantor files Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded, and the state's instructions explain that electronic filing through myCTREC is available in participating towns (DRS). Stamford is town code 135. Ask the Stamford city clerk's office whether the city is on the electronic system and whether any extra municipal rate applies.

sections.h2: When are Stamford property taxes due?
sections.html:
Connecticut leaves the schedule to each municipality. The legislature allows one, two or four installments and sets only an outer limit, which is that the final installment cannot be later than 45 days before the fiscal year closes (Chapter 204).

Stamford is a city governed by a Mayor and Board of Representatives, so mill rate decisions go through its budget process. Ask the Stamford Tax Collector for the installment dates and the Assessor for the current assessment, and request a payoff or proration figure before closing. If any installment is late, interest accrues at 18 percent a year under the statute, with a $2 minimum unless the city waives it.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale a good fit in Stamford?
sections.html:
It can be, especially for houses that need work or sellers who cannot wait. A cash offer does not depend on the buyer's mortgage, so it avoids a financing contingency that sometimes collapses late.

Because Stamford prices are high, compare carefully: a listing may net more if you can renovate and wait, while a cash sale gives certainty. We buy Stamford houses as-is and will explain the numbers either way.

faqs.a: Stamford is in Fairfield County, Connecticut, on Long Island Sound about 34 miles from New York City.

faqs.q: How many people live in Stamford?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 135,470 people, making Stamford the second most populous city in Connecticut.

faqs.q: How much is the conveyance tax when selling a house in Stamford?
faqs.a: On most homes it is one percent, with 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the city. The state rate rises to 1.25 percent on the part of a residential price above $800,000.

faqs.q: Can a Stamford house in a flood-prone area still sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Buyers and lenders will want the flood zone status and any insurance history, and a cash buyer can often work around those issues.

faqs.q: How long is the train ride from Stamford to Grand Central?
faqs.a: Wikipedia reports an average nonstop commute of 47 minutes on Metro-North.

faqs.q: Who sets Stamford's property tax installments?
faqs.a: Connecticut law lets each municipality choose one, two or four installments, so check with the Stamford Tax Collector for exact dates.
